solution:
(i) \(\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}, \vec{b}=-\hat{i}+5\hat{j}, \vec{c}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}, \vec{d}=-7\hat{i}+5\hat{j}\)
\(\vec{AB}=\vec{b}-\vec{a}=(-\hat{i}+5\hat{j})-(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j})=-3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}\)
\(\vec{CD}=\vec{d}-\vec{c}=(-7\hat{i}+5\hat{j})-(-\hat{i}+\hat{j})=-6\hat{i}+4\hat{j}\)
(ii) \(\vec{CD}=-6\hat{i}+4\hat{j}=2(-3\hat{i}+2\hat{j})=2\vec{AB}\), therefore \(\vec{CD}\) and \(\vec{AB}\) are parallel.
(iii) \(\vec{BE}=(k\hat{i}+\hat{j})-(-\hat{i}+5\hat{j})=(k+1)\hat{i}-4\hat{j}\)
\(\vec{AC}=(-\hat{i}+\hat{j})-(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j})=-3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}\)
\(\vec{BE}=m\vec{AC}\)
\((k+1)\hat{i}-4\hat{j}=m(-3\hat{i}-2\hat{j})\)
So \(-4=-2m\), \(m=2\)
and \(k+1=-3m\)
\(k+1=-3(2)\)
\(k=-6-1\)
\(k=-7\)

stem: The non-zero vectors \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are not collinear. Find the value of \(\lambda\) and \(\mu\): (i) \(\vec{a}+3\vec{b}=2\lambda\vec{a}-\mu\vec{b}\) (ii) \((1+\lambda)\vec{a}+2\lambda\vec{b}=\mu\vec{a}+4\mu\vec{b}\) (iii) \((3\lambda+5)\vec{a}+\vec{b}=2\mu\vec{a}+(\lambda-3)\vec{b}\)

stem: Are the following sets of vectors linearly independent? (i) \(\vec{a}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=3\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+9\hat{k}\) (ii) \(\vec{a}=-2\hat{i}-4\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\), \(\vec{c}=\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\). Interpret the results.
solution:
(i) \(\vec{a}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}, \vec{b}=3\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+9\hat{k}\)
\(\vec{b}=3(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\)
\(\vec{b}=3\vec{a}\). Here \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are linearly dependent vectors. Hence \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are collinear.
(ii) \(\vec{a}=-2\hat{i}-4\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\), \(\vec{c}=\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\)
Let \(x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}+z\vec{c}=\vec{0}\)
\(\therefore x(-2\hat{i}-4\hat{k})+y(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\hat{k})+z(\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+3\hat{k})=\vec{0}\)
\(-2x+y+z=0\)
\(-2y-4z=0\)
\(-4x-y+3z=0\)
\(\therefore x=0, y=0, z=0\). Here \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\) are linearly independent vectors.
Hence \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\) are non-coplanar.

solution:
(a) The distance from (2, 3, 4) to the XY plane is \(|z|=4\) units.

stem: Prove that the line segment joining the midpoints of two sides of a triangle is parallel to and half of the third side.
solution:
Let the triangle be ABC. If M and N are the midpoints of AB and AC respectively, then
\(\vec{AM}=\dfrac{1}{2}\vec{AB}\) and \(\vec{AN}=\dfrac{1}{2}\vec{AC}\). Thus by triangle law
\(\vec{AN}=\vec{AM}+\vec{MN}\)
\(\therefore \vec{MN}=\vec{AN}-\vec{AM}=\dfrac{\vec{AC}-\vec{AB}}{2}=\dfrac{\vec{BC}}{2}\)
Thus, \(\vec{MN}\) is parallel to and half as long as \(\vec{BC}\).

stem: In quadrilateral ABCD, M and N are the mid-points of the diagonals AC and BD respectively. Prove that \(\vec{AB}+\vec{AD}+\vec{CB}+\vec{CD}=4\vec{MN}\)
solution:
\(\vec{AB}=\vec{AM}+\vec{MN}+\vec{NB}\) ...(1)
\(\vec{AD}=\vec{AM}+\vec{MN}+\vec{ND}\) ...(2)
\(\vec{CB}=\vec{CM}+\vec{MN}+\vec{NB}\) ...(3)
\(\vec{CD}=\vec{CM}+\vec{MN}+\vec{ND}\) ...(4)
Add (1), (2), (3), (4) to get
\(\vec{AB}+\vec{AD}+\vec{CB}+\vec{CD}=2\vec{AM}+2\vec{CM}+4\vec{MN}+2\vec{NB}+2\vec{ND}\)
\(=2(\vec{AM}+\vec{CM})+4\vec{MN}+2(\vec{NB}+\vec{ND})\)
\(=2(\vec{AM}-\vec{AM})+4\vec{MN}+2(\vec{NB}-\vec{NB})\) (since M, N are midpoints, \(\vec{MC}=\vec{AM}\) and \(\vec{DN}=\vec{NB}\))
\(=2(\vec{0})+4\vec{MN}+2(\vec{0})\)
\(=4\vec{MN}\)

stem: Express \(-\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\) as the linear combination of the vectors \(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-4\hat{k}\), \(2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\) and \(3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).
solution:
Let \(\vec{r}=-\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\), \(\vec{a}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-4\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\), \(\vec{c}=3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\)
Consider \(\vec{r}=x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}+z\vec{c}\)

Using Cramer's rule we get, \(x=2, y=2, z=3\). Therefore \(\vec{r}=2\vec{a}+2\vec{b}-3\vec{c}\)

stem: Show that the three points A(1, -2, 3), B(2, 3, -4) and C(0, -7, 10) are collinear.
solution:
If \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\) are the position vectors of the points A, B and C respectively, then

\(\vec{AC}=\vec{c}-\vec{a}=-\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+7\hat{k}=(-1)[\hat{i}+5\hat{j}-7\hat{k}]\)
\(\vec{AC}=(-1)\vec{AB}\) ...from (1)
That is, \(\vec{AC}\) is a scalar multiple of \(\vec{AB}\). Therefore, they are parallel. But point A is in common. Hence, the points A, B and C are collinear.

stem: Show that the vectors \(4\hat{i}+13\hat{j}-18\hat{k}\), \(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\) and \(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k}\) are coplanar.
solution:
Let \(\vec{a}=4\hat{i}+13\hat{j}-18\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\), \(\vec{c}=2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k}\)
Consider \(\vec{a}=m\vec{b}+n\vec{c}\)
\(\therefore 4\hat{i}+13\hat{j}-18\hat{k}=m(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})+n(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k})\)
\(\therefore 4\hat{i}+13\hat{j}-18\hat{k}=(m+2n)\hat{i}+(-2m+3n)\hat{j}+(3m-4n)\hat{k}\)
By equality of two vectors, we have
\(m+2n=4\) ...(1)
\(-2m+3n=13\) ...(2)
\(3m-4n=-18\) ...(3)
Solving (1) and (2) we get, \(\therefore m=-2, n=3\)
These values of m and n satisfy equation (3) also.
\(\therefore \vec{a}=-2\vec{b}+3\vec{c}\)
Therefore, \(\vec{a}\) is a linear combination of \(\vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\). Hence, \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\) are coplanar.

context: Find the co-ordinates of the point which divides the line segment joining the points A(2, –6, 8) and B(–1, 3, –4).
stem: (i) Internally in the ratio 1 : 3.
solution:
Let \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) be position vectors of the points A and B respectively.
\(\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} + 8\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{b} = -\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}\).
Suppose R(\(\vec{r}\)) is the point which divides the line segment joining A(\(\vec{a}\)) and B(\(\vec{b}\)) internally in the ratio 1 : 3, then
\(\vec{r} = \dfrac{1(\vec{b}) + 3(\vec{a})}{1+3} = \dfrac{-1(\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k}) + 3(2\hat{i}-6\hat{j}+8\hat{k})}{4}\)
\(\therefore \vec{r} = \dfrac{5\hat{i} - 15\hat{j} + 20\hat{k}}{4}\)
Therefore, the coordinates of the point R are \(\left(\dfrac{5}{4}, \dfrac{-15}{4}, 5\right)\).

context: Find the co-ordinates of the point which divides the line segment joining the points A(2, –6, 8) and B(–1, 3, –4).

Therefore, the coordinates of the point S are \(\left(\dfrac{7}{2}, \dfrac{-21}{2}, 14\right)\).

stem: If the three points A(3, 2, p), B(q, 8, –10), C(–2, –3, 1) are collinear then find (i) the ratio in which the point C divides the line segment AB, (ii) the values of p and q.
solution:
Let \(\vec{a} = 3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+p\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = q\hat{i}+8\hat{j}-10\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{c} = -2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
Suppose the point C divides the line segment AB in the ratio t : 1, then by section formula, \(\vec{c} = \dfrac{t\vec{b} + 1\vec{a}}{t+1}\).
\(\therefore -2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k} = \dfrac{t(q\hat{i}+8\hat{j}-10\hat{k}) + 1(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+p\hat{k})}{t+1}\)
\(\therefore (-2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k})(t+1) = (tq+3)\hat{i}+(8t+2)\hat{j}+(-10t+p)\hat{k}\)
\(\therefore -2(t+1)\hat{i} - 3(t+1)\hat{j} + (t+1)\hat{k} = (tq+3)\hat{i}+(8t+2)\hat{j}+(-10t+p)\hat{k}\)
Using equality of two vectors:
\(-2(t+1) = tq+3\) ... (1)
\(-3(t+1) = 8t+2\) ... (2)
\(t+1 = -10t+p\) ... (3)
Now equation (2) gives \(t = -\dfrac{5}{11}\).
Put \(t = -\dfrac{5}{11}\) in equations (1) and (3), we get \(q = 9\) and \(p = -4\).
The negative sign of t suggests that the point C divides the line segment AB externally in the ratio 5 : 11.

stem: If A(5, 1, p), B(1, q, p) and C(1, –2, 3) are vertices of a triangle and \(G\left(r, -\dfrac{4}{3}, \dfrac{1}{3}\right)\) is its centroid, then find the values of p, q and r.
solution:
Let \(\vec{a} = 5\hat{i}+\hat{j}+p\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = \hat{i}+q\hat{j}+p\hat{k}\), \(\vec{c} = \hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{g} = r\hat{i}-\dfrac{4}{3}\hat{j}+\dfrac{1}{3}\hat{k}\).
By the centroid formula, \(\vec{g} = \dfrac{\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}}{3}\).
\(\therefore 3\vec{g} = \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}\)
\(\therefore 3\left(r\hat{i}-\dfrac{4}{3}\hat{j}+\dfrac{1}{3}\hat{k}\right) = (5\hat{i}+\hat{j}+p\hat{k})+(\hat{i}+q\hat{j}+p\hat{k})+(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\)
\(\therefore (3r)\hat{i} - 4\hat{j} + \hat{k} = 7\hat{i}+(q-1)\hat{j}+(2p+3)\hat{k}\)
\(\therefore 3r = 7,\ -4 = q-1,\ 1 = 2p+3\)
\(\therefore r = \dfrac{7}{3},\ q = -3,\ p = -1\).

stem: If \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\), \(\vec{c}\) are the position vectors of the points A, B, C respectively and \(5\vec{a} - 3\vec{b} - 2\vec{c} = \vec{0}\), then find the ratio in which the point C divides the line segment BA.
solution:
As \(5\vec{a} - 3\vec{b} - 2\vec{c} = \vec{0}\)
\(\therefore 2\vec{c} = 5\vec{a} - 3\vec{b}\)
\(\therefore \vec{c} = \dfrac{5\vec{a}-3\vec{b}}{2}\)
\(\therefore \vec{c} = \dfrac{5\vec{a}-3\vec{b}}{5-3}\)
This shows that the point C divides BA externally in the ratio 5 : 3.

stem: Prove that the medians of a triangle are concurrent.
solution:
Let A, B and C be vertices of a triangle. Let D, E and F be the mid-points of the sides BC, AC and AB respectively. Let \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\), \(\vec{c}\), \(\vec{d}\), \(\vec{e}\) and \(\vec{f}\) be position vectors of points A, B, C, D, E and F respectively.
Therefore, by mid-point formula,
\(\vec{d} = \dfrac{\vec{b}+\vec{c}}{2}\), \(\vec{e} = \dfrac{\vec{a}+\vec{c}}{2}\) and \(\vec{f} = \dfrac{\vec{a}+\vec{b}}{2}\)
\(\therefore 2\vec{d} = \vec{b}+\vec{c}\), \(2\vec{e} = \vec{a}+\vec{c}\) and \(2\vec{f} = \vec{a}+\vec{b}\)
\(\therefore 2\vec{d}+\vec{a} = \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}\), similarly \(2\vec{e}+\vec{b} = 2\vec{f}+\vec{c} = \vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}\)
\(\therefore \dfrac{2\vec{d}+\vec{a}}{3} = \dfrac{2\vec{e}+\vec{b}}{3} = \dfrac{2\vec{f}+\vec{c}}{3} = \dfrac{\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}}{3} = \vec{g}\) (say)
Then we have \(\vec{g} = \dfrac{\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}}{3} = \dfrac{(2)\vec{d}+(1)\vec{a}}{2+1} = \dfrac{(2)\vec{e}+(1)\vec{b}}{2+1} = \dfrac{(2)\vec{f}+(1)\vec{c}}{2+1}\)
If G is the point whose position vector is \(\vec{g}\), then from the above equation it is clear that the point G lies on the medians AD, BE, CF and it divides each of the medians AD, BE, CF internally in the ratio 2 : 1.
Therefore, three medians are concurrent.

stem: Prove that the angle bisectors of a triangle are concurrent.
solution:
Let A, B and C be vertices of a triangle. Let AD, BE and CF be the angle bisectors of the triangle ABC. Let \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\), \(\vec{c}\), \(\vec{d}\), \(\vec{e}\) and \(\vec{f}\) be the position vectors of the points A, B, C, D, E and F respectively. Also AB = z, BC = x, AC = y. Now, the angle bisector AD meets the side BC at the point D. Therefore, the point D divides the line segment BC internally in the ratio AB : AC, that is z : y.
Hence, by section formula for internal division, we have \(\vec{d} = \dfrac{z\vec{c}+y\vec{b}}{z+y}\)
Similarly, we get \(\vec{e} = \dfrac{x\vec{a}+z\vec{c}}{x+z}\) and \(\vec{f} = \dfrac{y\vec{b}+x\vec{a}}{y+x}\)
As \(\vec{d} = \dfrac{z\vec{c}+y\vec{b}}{z+y}\)
\(\therefore (z+y)\vec{d} = z\vec{c}+y\vec{b}\)
i.e. \((z+y)\vec{d} + x\vec{a} = x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}+z\vec{c}\)
similarly \((x+z)\vec{e} + y\vec{b} = x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}+z\vec{c}\)
and \((x+y)\vec{f} + z\vec{c} = x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}+z\vec{c}\)
\(\therefore \dfrac{(z+y)\vec{d}+x\vec{a}}{x+y+z} = \dfrac{(x+z)\vec{e}+y\vec{b}}{x+y+z} = \dfrac{(x+y)\vec{f}+z\vec{c}}{x+y+z} = \dfrac{x\vec{a}+y\vec{b}+z\vec{c}}{x+y+z} = \vec{h}\) (say)
Then we have \(\vec{h} = \dfrac{(y+z)\vec{d}+x\vec{a}}{(y+z)+x} = \dfrac{(x+z)\vec{e}+y\vec{b}}{(x+z)+y} = \dfrac{(x+y)\vec{f}+z\vec{c}}{(x+y)+z}\)
That is, point H(\(\vec{h}\)) divides AD in the ratio (y+z) : x, BE in the ratio (x+z) : y and CF in the ratio (x+y) : z.
This shows that the point H is the point of concurrence of the angle bisectors AD, BE and CF of the triangle ABC. Thus, the angle bisectors of a triangle are concurrent and H is called the incentre of the triangle ABC.

stem: Using vector method, find the incenter of the triangle whose vertices are A(0, 3, 0), B(0, 0, 4) and C(0, 3, 4).
solution:
Let \(\vec{a} = 3\hat{j}\), \(\vec{b} = 4\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{c} = 3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\)
\(\therefore \vec{AB} = \vec{b}-\vec{a} = -3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\), \(\vec{AC} = \vec{c}-\vec{a} = 4\hat{k}\), \(\vec{BC} = \vec{c}-\vec{b} = 3\hat{j}\)
\(\therefore |\vec{AB}| = 5, |\vec{AC}| = 4, |\vec{BC}| = 3\)
If H(\(\vec{h}\)) is the incenter of triangle ABC then,
\(\vec{h} = \dfrac{|\vec{BC}|\vec{a}+|\vec{AC}|\vec{b}+|\vec{AB}|\vec{c}}{|\vec{BC}|+|\vec{AC}|+|\vec{AB}|}\)
\(\therefore \vec{h} = \dfrac{3(3\hat{j})+4(4\hat{k})+5(3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})}{3+4+5}\)
\(= \dfrac{9\hat{j}+16\hat{k}+15\hat{j}+20\hat{k}}{12}\)
\(\therefore \vec{h} = \dfrac{24\hat{j}+36\hat{k}}{12}\)
\(\therefore \vec{h} = 2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\)
And H \(\equiv (0, 2, 3)\).

stem: If \(4\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+8\hat{k}\), \(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\) and \(2\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+7\hat{k}\) are the position vectors of the vertices A, B and C respectively of triangle ABC, find the position vector of the point in which the bisector of \(\angle A\) meets BC.
solution:
\(\vec{a} = 4\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+8\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = 2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\), \(\vec{c} = 2\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+7\hat{k}\)
\(\vec{AC} = \vec{c}-\vec{a} = -2\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\)
\(\vec{AB} = \vec{b}-\vec{a} = -2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}-4\hat{k}\)
\(\therefore |\vec{AB}| = \sqrt{4+16+16} = 6\) units
\(\therefore |\vec{AC}| = \sqrt{4+4+1} = 3\) units
Let D be the point where the angle bisector of \(\angle A\) meets BC.
D divides BC in the ratio AB : AC
i.e. \(\vec{d} = \dfrac{|\vec{AB}|\vec{c}+|\vec{AC}|\vec{b}}{|\vec{AB}|+|\vec{AC}|}\)
\(= \dfrac{6(2\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+7\hat{k})+3(2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k})}{6+3}\)
\(= \dfrac{(12\hat{i}+30\hat{j}+42\hat{k})+(6\hat{i}+9\hat{j}+12\hat{k})}{9}\)
\(= \dfrac{18\hat{i}+39\hat{j}+54\hat{k}}{9}\)
\(\therefore \vec{d} = 2\hat{i}+\dfrac{13}{3}\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\).

stem: If G(a, 2, –1) is the centroid of the triangle with vertices P(1, 3, 2), Q(3, b, –4) and R(5, 1, c), then find the values of a, b and c.
solution:
As G(\(\vec{g}\)) is the centroid of \(\triangle PQR\), \(\vec{g} = \dfrac{\vec{p}+\vec{q}+\vec{r}}{3}\)
\(a\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k} = \dfrac{(\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+(3\hat{i}+b\hat{j}-4\hat{k})+(5\hat{i}+\hat{j}+c\hat{k})}{3} = \dfrac{(1+3+5)\hat{i}+(3+b+1)\hat{j}+(2-4+c)\hat{k}}{3}\)
By equality of vectors,
\(a = \dfrac{1+3+5}{3} = \dfrac{9}{3} = 3 \therefore a = 3\)
\(2 = \dfrac{3+b+1}{3} \therefore 6 = 4+b \therefore b = 2\)
\(-1 = \dfrac{2-4+c}{3} \therefore -3 = -2+c \therefore c = -1\).

stem: Find the centroid of the tetrahedron with vertices A(3, –5, 7), B(5, 4, 2), C(7, –7, –3), D(1, 0, 2).
solution:
Let \(\vec{a} = 3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+7\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = 5\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), \(\vec{c} = 7\hat{i}-7\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\), \(\vec{d} = \hat{i}+2\hat{k}\) be position vectors of vertices A, B, C and D.
By the centroid formula, centroid G(\(\vec{g}\)) is given by
\(\vec{g} = \dfrac{\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}+\vec{d}}{4}\)
\(= \dfrac{(3\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+7\hat{k})+(5\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+2\hat{k})+(7\hat{i}-7\hat{j}-3\hat{k})+(\hat{i}+2\hat{k})}{4}\)
\(= \dfrac{(3+5+7+1)\hat{i}+(-5+4-7+0)\hat{j}+(7+2-3+2)\hat{k}}{4} = \dfrac{16\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+8\hat{k}}{4}\)
\(= 4\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\)
Therefore, the centroid of the tetrahedron is G \(\equiv (4, -2, 2)\).

stem: Find the ratio in which point P divides AB and CD where A(2, –3, 4), B(0, 5, 2), C(–1, 5, 3) and D(2, –1, 3). Also, find its coordinates.
solution:
Let point P divide AB in ratio m : 1 and CD in ratio n : 1.
By section formula,
\(P \equiv \left(\dfrac{2}{m+1}, \dfrac{5m-3}{m+1}, \dfrac{2m+4}{m+1}\right) \equiv \left(\dfrac{2n-1}{n+1}, \dfrac{n+5}{n+1}, \dfrac{3n+3}{n+1}\right)\)
Equating z-coordinates,
\(\dfrac{2m+4}{m+1} = \dfrac{3n+3}{n+1}\)
\(\therefore \dfrac{2m+4}{m+1} = \dfrac{3(n+1)}{(n+1)}\)
\(\therefore 2m+4 = 3(m+1)\)
\(\therefore 2m+4 = 3m+3\)
\(\therefore 1 = m\)
Also, by equating x-coordinates,
\(\dfrac{2}{m+1} = \dfrac{2n-1}{n+1}\)
\(\dfrac{2}{1+1} = \dfrac{2n-1}{n+1}\quad (m=1)\)
\(\therefore n+1 = 2n-1\)
\(\therefore 2 = n\)
P divides AB in ratio m : 1 i.e. 1 : 1 and CD in the ratio n : 1 i.e. 2 : 1.
\(P \equiv \left(\dfrac{2}{1+1}, \dfrac{5-3}{1+1}, \dfrac{2+4}{1+1}\right) \equiv (1, 1, 3)\).

stem: In a triangle ABC, D and E are points on BC and AC respectively, such that BD = 2DC and AE = 3EC. Let P be the point of intersection of AD and BE. Find BP/PF using vector methods.
solution:
Let \(\vec{a}\), \(\vec{b}\), \(\vec{c}\) be the position vectors of A, B and C respectively with respect to some origin.
D divides BC in the ratio 2 : 1 and E divides AC in the ratio 3 : 1.
\(\therefore \vec{d} = \dfrac{\vec{b}+2\vec{c}}{3}\), \(\vec{e} = \dfrac{\vec{a}+3\vec{c}}{4}\)
Let the point of intersection P of AD and BE divide BE in the ratio k : 1 and AD in the ratio m : 1, then the position vectors of P in these two cases are \(\dfrac{\vec{b}+k\left(\dfrac{\vec{a}+3\vec{c}}{4}\right)}{k+1}\) and \(\dfrac{\vec{a}+m\left(\dfrac{\vec{b}+2\vec{c}}{3}\right)}{m+1}\) respectively.
Equating the position vectors of P we get,
\(\dfrac{k}{4(k+1)}\vec{a} + \dfrac{1}{k+1}\vec{b} + \dfrac{3k}{4(k+1)}\vec{c} = \dfrac{1}{m+1}\vec{a} + \dfrac{m}{3(m+1)}\vec{b} + \dfrac{2m}{3(m+1)}\vec{c}\)
\(\therefore \dfrac{k}{4(k+1)} = \dfrac{1}{m+1}\) ... (1)
\(\dfrac{1}{k+1} = \dfrac{m}{3(m+1)}\) ... (2)
\(\dfrac{3k}{4(k+1)} = \dfrac{2m}{3(m+1)}\) ... (3)
Dividing (3) by (2) we get,
\(\dfrac{3k}{4} = 2\) i.e. \(k = \dfrac{8}{3}\)
therefore \(\dfrac{BP}{PF} = k:1 = 8:3\).

stem: If \(\vec{a} = \hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{b} = 3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) find the angle between the vectors \(2\vec{a}+\vec{b}\) and \(\vec{a}+2\vec{b}\).
solution: \(2\vec{a}+\vec{b} = 2\left(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\right)+\left(3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\right) = 5\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k} = \vec{m}\) (say). \(\vec{a}+2\vec{b} = \left(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\right)+2\left(3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\right) = 7\hat{i}+\hat{k} = \vec{n}\) (say). \(\therefore \vec{m}\cdot\vec{n} = (2\vec{a}+\vec{b})\cdot(\vec{a}+2\vec{b}) = \left(5\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-4\hat{k}\right)\cdot\left(7\hat{i}+\hat{k}\right) = (5)(7)+(3)(0)+(-4)(1) = 31\). \(|\vec{m}| = \sqrt{(5)^2+(3)^2+(-4)^2} = \sqrt{50}\). \(|\vec{n}| = \sqrt{(7)^2+(0)^2+(1)^2} = \sqrt{50}\). If \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec{m}\) and \(\vec{n}\) then \(\cos\theta = \frac{\vec{m}\cdot\vec{n}}{|\vec{m}||\vec{n}|} = \frac{31}{\sqrt{50}\times\sqrt{50}} = \frac{31}{50}\). \(\therefore \theta = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{31}{50}\right)\).

stem: If a line makes angle \(90^\circ, 60^\circ\) and \(30^\circ\) with the positive direction of X, Y and Z axes respectively, find its direction cosines.

stem: Find the vector projection of \(\vec{PQ}\) on \(\vec{AB}\) where P, Q, A, B are the points \((-2, 1, 3)\), \((3, 2, 5)\), \((4, -3, 5)\) and \((7, -5, -1)\) respectively.
solution: Let the position vectors of P, Q, A, B be \(\vec{p}, \vec{q}, \vec{a}, \vec{b}\) respectively. \(\vec{p} = -2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\), \(\vec{q} = 3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\), \(\vec{a} = 4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = 7\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-\hat{k}\). \(\therefore \vec{PQ} = \vec{q}-\vec{p} = \left(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\right)-\left(-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\right) = 5\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\). And \(\vec{AB} = \vec{b}-\vec{a} = \left(7\hat{i}-5\hat{j}-\hat{k}\right)-\left(4\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\right) = 3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-6\hat{k}\). \(\therefore\) Vector projection of \(\vec{PQ}\) on \(\vec{AB}\) \(= \frac{\vec{PQ}\cdot\vec{AB}}{|\vec{AB}|^2}\vec{AB} = \frac{(5)(3)+(1)(-2)+(2)(-6)}{(3)^2+(-2)^2+(-6)^2}\vec{AB} = \frac{1}{49}\left(3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-6\hat{k}\right) = \frac{3}{49}\hat{i}-\frac{2}{49}\hat{j}-\frac{6}{49}\hat{k}\).

stem: Find the values of \(\lambda\) for which the angle between the vectors \(\vec{a} = 2\lambda^2\hat{i}+4\lambda\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{b} = 7\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}\) is obtuse.
solution: If \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\), then \(\cos\theta = \frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|}\). If \(\theta\) is obtuse then \(\cos\theta < 0\). \(\therefore \frac{\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}||\vec{b}|} < 0\) i.e. \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} < 0\) \(\left[\because |\vec{a}||\vec{b}| > 0\right]\). \(\therefore \left(2\lambda^2\hat{i}+4\lambda\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)\cdot\left(7\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\lambda\hat{k}\right) < 0\). \(\therefore 14\lambda^2-8\lambda+\lambda < 0\) i.e. \(14\lambda^2-7\lambda < 0\). \(\therefore 7\lambda(2\lambda-1) < 0\) i.e. \(\lambda\left(\lambda-\frac{1}{2}\right) < 0\) i.e. \(0 < \lambda < \frac{1}{2}\). Thus the angle between \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) is obtuse if \(0 < \lambda < \frac{1}{2}\).

stem: Find the direction cosines of the vector \(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\).
solution: Let \(\vec{a} = 2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}\). \(\therefore |\vec{a}| = \sqrt{(2)^2+(2)^2+(-1)^2} = \sqrt{9} = 3\). \(\therefore \hat{a} = \frac{\vec{a}}{|\vec{a}|} = \frac{2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k}}{3} = \frac{2}{3}\hat{i}+\frac{2}{3}\hat{j}-\frac{1}{3}\hat{k}\). \(\therefore\) The direction cosines of \(\vec{a}\) are \(\frac{2}{3}, \frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{3}\).

stem: Find the position vector of a point P such that \(\vec{AB}\) is inclined to the X axis at \(45^\circ\) and to the Y axis at \(60^\circ\), and \(OP = 12\) units.
solution: We have \(l = \cos 45^\circ = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), \(m = \cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\), \(n = \cos\gamma\). Now \(l^2+m^2+n^2 = 1\). \(\therefore \frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4}+\cos^2\gamma = 1\), i.e. \(\cos^2\gamma = \frac{1}{4}\), i.e. \(n = \cos\gamma = \pm\frac{1}{2}\). Now \(\vec{r} = |\vec{r}|\hat{r} = |\vec{r}|\left(l\hat{i}+m\hat{j}+n\hat{k}\right) = 12\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{i}+\frac{1}{2}\hat{j}\pm\frac{1}{2}\hat{k}\right)\). Hence \(\vec{r} = 6\sqrt{2}\hat{i}+6\hat{j}\pm6\hat{k}\).

stem: A line makes angles of measure \(45^\circ\) and \(60^\circ\) with the positive direction of the Y and Z axes respectively. Find the angle made by the line with the positive direction of the X-axis.
solution: Let \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) be the angles made by the line with the positive direction of X, Y and Z axes respectively. Given \(\beta = 45^\circ\) and \(\gamma = 60^\circ\). Now \(\cos\beta = \cos 45^\circ\) and \(\cos\gamma = \cos 60^\circ = \frac{1}{2}\). \(\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma = 1\). \(\therefore \cos^2\alpha+\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{4} = 1\). \(\therefore \cos^2\alpha = \frac{1}{4}\). \(\therefore \cos\alpha = \pm\frac{1}{2}\). \(\therefore \alpha = 60^\circ\) or \(120^\circ\). There are two lines satisfying the given conditions. Their direction angles are \(45^\circ, 60^\circ, 60^\circ\) and \(45^\circ, 60^\circ, 120^\circ\).

stem: A line passes through the points \((6, -7, -1)\) and \((2, -3, 1)\). Find the direction ratios and the direction cosines of the line so that the angle \(\alpha\) is acute.
solution: Let A\((6, -7, -1)\) and B\((2, -3, 1)\) be the given points. So \(\vec{a} = 6\hat{i}-7\hat{j}-\hat{k}, \vec{b} = 2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}\). \(\vec{AB} = \vec{b}-\vec{a} = (2-6)\hat{i}+(-3+7)\hat{j}+(1+1)\hat{k} = -4\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\). The direction ratios of \(\vec{AB}\) are \(-4, 4, 2\). Let the direction cosines of \(\vec{AB}\) be \(-4k, 4k, 2k\). Then \((-4k)^2+(4k)^2+(2k)^2 = 1\) i.e. \(16k^2+16k^2+4k^2 = 1\) i.e. \(36k^2 = 1\) i.e. \(k = \pm\frac{1}{6}\). Since the line AB is so directed that the angle \(\alpha\) which it makes with the X-axis is acute, \(\therefore \cos\alpha = -4k > 0\). \(\therefore\) As \(k < 0\), \(\therefore k = -\frac{1}{6}\). \(\therefore\) The direction cosines of \(\vec{AB}\) are \(-4\left(-\frac{1}{6}\right), 4\left(-\frac{1}{6}\right), 2\left(-\frac{1}{6}\right)\) i.e. \(\frac{2}{3}, \frac{-2}{3}, \frac{-1}{3}\).

stem: Prove that the altitudes of a triangle are concurrent.
solution: Let A, B and C be the vertices of a triangle. Let AD, BE and CF be the altitudes of the triangle ABC, therefore \(AD \perp BC\), \(BE \perp AC\), \(CF \perp AB\). Let \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}, \vec{d}, \vec{e}, \vec{f}\) be the position vectors of A, B, C, D, E, F respectively. Let P be the point of intersection of the altitudes AD and BE with \(\vec{p}\) as the position vector. Therefore, \(\vec{AP}\perp\vec{BC}, \vec{BP}\perp\vec{AC}\) .......(1). To show that the altitudes AD, BE and CF are concurrent, it is sufficient to show that the altitude CF passes through the point P. We will have to prove that \(\vec{CF}\) and \(\vec{CP}\) are collinear vectors. This can be achieved by showing \(\vec{CP}\perp\vec{AB}\). Now from (1) we have \(\vec{AP}\perp\vec{BC}\) and \(\vec{BP}\perp\vec{AC}\). \(\therefore \vec{AP}\cdot\vec{BC} = 0\) and \(\vec{BP}\cdot\vec{AC} = 0\). \(\therefore (\vec{p}-\vec{a})\cdot(\vec{c}-\vec{b}) = 0\) and \((\vec{p}-\vec{b})\cdot(\vec{c}-\vec{a}) = 0\). \(\therefore \vec{p}\cdot\vec{c}-\vec{p}\cdot\vec{b}-\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c}+\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 0\) .....(2). \(\vec{p}\cdot\vec{c}-\vec{p}\cdot\vec{a}-\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}+\vec{b}\cdot\vec{a} = 0\) ......(3). Therefore, subtracting equation (2) from equation (3), we get \(-\vec{p}\cdot\vec{a}+\vec{p}\cdot\vec{b}-\vec{b}\cdot\vec{c}+\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c} = 0\) (Since \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=\vec{b}\cdot\vec{a}\)). \(\therefore \vec{p}(\vec{b}-\vec{a})-\vec{c}(\vec{b}-\vec{a}) = 0\). \(\therefore (\vec{p}-\vec{c})\cdot(\vec{b}-\vec{a}) = 0\). \(\therefore \vec{CP}\cdot\vec{AB} = 0\). \(\therefore \vec{CP}\perp\vec{AB}\). Hence the proof.

context: Find the cross product \(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\) and verify that it is orthogonal (perpendicular) to both \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\).
stem: \(\vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}\), \(\vec{b} = 2\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 6\hat{k}\)
solution: \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&1&-1\\2&4&6\end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}1&-1\\4&6\end{vmatrix}\hat{i} - \begin{vmatrix}1&-1\\2&6\end{vmatrix}\hat{j} + \begin{vmatrix}1&1\\2&4\end{vmatrix}\hat{k}\) \(= [6-(-4)]\hat{i} - [6-(-2)]\hat{j} + (4-2)\hat{k} = 10\hat{i} - 8\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}\). Now \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\cdot\vec{a} = (10\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\cdot(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}) = 10-8-2=0\) and \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\cdot\vec{b} = (10\hat{i}-8\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\cdot(2\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+6\hat{k}) = 20-32+12=0\). So \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\) is orthogonal to both \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\).

context: Find the cross product \(\vec{a} \times \vec{b}\) and verify that it is orthogonal (perpendicular) to both \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\).

solution: \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&3&-2\\-1&0&5\end{vmatrix} = \begin{vmatrix}3&-2\\0&5\end{vmatrix}\hat{i} - \begin{vmatrix}1&-2\\-1&5\end{vmatrix}\hat{j} + \begin{vmatrix}1&3\\-1&0\end{vmatrix}\hat{k} = (15-0)\hat{i} - (5-2)\hat{j} + [0-(-3)]\hat{k} = 15\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\). Now \((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\cdot\vec{a}=(15\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\cdot(\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-2\hat{k})=15-9-6=0\), and \((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\cdot\vec{b}=(15\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\cdot(-\hat{i}+5\hat{k})=-15+0+15=0\), so \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}\) is orthogonal to both \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\).

stem: Find all vectors of magnitude \(10\sqrt{3}\) that are perpendicular to the plane of \(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\).
solution: Let \(\vec{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{b}=-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\). Then \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\1&2&1\\-1&3&4\end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(8-3)-\hat{j}(4+1)+\hat{k}(3+2)=5\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+5\hat{k}=\vec{m}\) (say). \(\therefore |\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|=\sqrt{(5)^2+(-5)^2+(5)^2}=\sqrt{3(5)^2}=5\sqrt{3}=|\vec{m}|\). Therefore, the unit vector perpendicular to the plane of \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) is given by \(\hat{m}=\dfrac{\vec{m}}{|\vec{m}|}=\dfrac{\vec{a}\times\vec{b}}{|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|}=\dfrac{5\hat{i}-5\hat{j}+5\hat{k}}{5\sqrt{3}}=\dfrac{\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{3}}\). Hence, the vectors of magnitude \(10\sqrt{3}\) that are perpendicular to the plane of \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\) are \(\pm 10\sqrt{3}\,\hat{m}=\pm 10\sqrt{3}\left(\dfrac{\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{3}}\right)\), i.e. \(\pm 10(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k})\).

stem: If \(\vec{u}+\vec{v}+\vec{w}=\vec{0}\), show that \(\vec{u}\times\vec{v}=\vec{v}\times\vec{w}=\vec{w}\times\vec{u}\).
solution: Suppose that \(\vec{u}+\vec{v}+\vec{w}=\vec{0}\). Then \((\vec{u}+\vec{v}+\vec{w})\times\vec{v}=\vec{0}\times\vec{v}\) i.e. \(\vec{u}\times\vec{v}+\vec{v}\times\vec{v}+\vec{w}\times\vec{v}=\vec{0}\). But \(\vec{v}\times\vec{v}=\vec{0}\). Thus \(\vec{u}\times\vec{v}+\vec{w}\times\vec{v}=\vec{0}\). Thus \(\vec{u}\times\vec{v}=-\vec{w}\times\vec{v}=\vec{v}\times\vec{w}\). Similarly, we have \(\vec{v}\times\vec{w}=\vec{w}\times\vec{u}\). Hence \(\vec{u}\times\vec{v}=\vec{v}\times\vec{w}=\vec{w}\times\vec{u}\).

stem: If \(\vec{a}=3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{c}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), find \((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{c}\) and \(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})\) and hence show that \((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{c}\neq\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})\).
solution: \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\3&-1&2\\2&1&-1\end{vmatrix}=-\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\). \((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{c}=(-\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+5\hat{k})\times(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\-1&7&5\\1&-2&2\end{vmatrix}=24\hat{i}+7\hat{j}-5\hat{k}\) ....(1). Now, \(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\2&1&-1\\1&-2&2\end{vmatrix}=-5\hat{j}-5\hat{k}\). \(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})=(3\hat{i}-\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\times(-5\hat{j}-5\hat{k})=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\3&-1&2\\0&-5&-5\end{vmatrix}=15(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k})\) ....(2). From (1) and (2), we conclude that \((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{c}\neq\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})\).

stem: Find the area of the triangle with vertices (1,2,0), (1,0,2), and (0,3,1).
solution: If \(A=(1,2,0)\), \(B=(1,0,2)\) and \(C=(0,3,1)\), then \(\overline{AB}=-2\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\), \(\overline{AC}=-\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and the area of triangle ABC is \(\dfrac{1}{2}|\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}|\). \(\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\0&-2&2\\-1&1&1\end{vmatrix}=-4\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\). \(\dfrac{|\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}|}{2}=\dfrac{|-4\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-2\hat{k}|}{2}=\dfrac{\sqrt{16+4+4}}{2}=\dfrac{\sqrt{24}}{2}=\dfrac{2\sqrt{6}}{2}=\sqrt{6}\) sq. units.

stem: Find the area of the parallelogram with vertices K(1, 2, 3), L(1, 3, 6), M(3, 8, 6) and N(3, 7, 3).

stem: Show that \((\vec{a}-\vec{b})\times(\vec{a}+\vec{b}) = 2(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\).
solution: Using distributive property, \((\vec{a}-\vec{b})\times(\vec{a}+\vec{b})=\vec{a}\times\vec{a}+\vec{a}\times\vec{b}-\vec{b}\times\vec{a}-\vec{b}\times\vec{b}\) (\(\because \vec{a}\times\vec{b}=-\vec{b}\times\vec{a}\)) \(=\vec{0}+\vec{a}\times\vec{b}+\vec{a}\times\vec{b}-\vec{0}\) (\(\because \vec{a}\times\vec{a}=\vec{0}\)) \(=2(\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\).

stem: Show that the three points with position vectors \(3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\), \(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(-\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\) respectively are collinear.
solution: Let A, B, C be the given three points. \(\vec{a}=3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\), \(\vec{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\vec{c}=-\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\). To show that points A, B, C are collinear. Now \(\overline{AB}=\vec{b}-\vec{a}=-2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\), \(\overline{AC}=\vec{c}-\vec{a}=-4\hat{i}+6\hat{j}-6\hat{k}\). \(\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\-2&3&-3\\-4&6&-6\end{vmatrix}=(-18+18)\hat{i}-(12-12)\hat{j}+(-12+12)\hat{k}=0\hat{i}-0\hat{j}+0\hat{k}=\vec{0}\). Vectors \(\overline{AB}\) and \(\overline{AC}\) are collinear, but the point A is common, therefore points A, B, C are collinear.

stem: Find a unit vector perpendicular to \(\overline{PQ}\) and \(\overline{PR}\) where \(P\equiv(2,2,0)\), \(Q\equiv(0,3,5)\) and \(R\equiv(5,0,3)\). Also find the sine of angle between \(\overline{PQ}\) and \(\overline{PR}\).
solution: \(\overline{PQ}=\vec{q}-\vec{p}=-2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\) and \(\overline{PR}=\vec{r}-\vec{p}=3\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\). Now \(|\overline{PQ}|=\sqrt{4+1+25}=\sqrt{30}\) and \(|\overline{PR}|=\sqrt{9+4+9}=\sqrt{22}\). \(\therefore \overline{PQ}\times\overline{PR}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\-2&1&5\\3&-2&3\end{vmatrix}=(3+10)\hat{i}-(-6-15)\hat{j}+(4-3)\hat{k}=13\hat{i}+21\hat{j}+\hat{k}\). \(\therefore |\overline{PQ}\times\overline{PR}|=\sqrt{169+441+1}=\sqrt{611}\). If \(\hat{n}\) is a unit vector perpendicular to \(\overline{PQ}\) and \(\overline{PR}\), then \(\hat{n}=\dfrac{\overline{PQ}\times\overline{PR}}{|\overline{PQ}\times\overline{PR}|}=\dfrac{13\hat{i}+21\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{611}}\). If \(\theta\) is the angle between \(\overline{PQ}\) and \(\overline{PR}\) then \(\sin\theta=\dfrac{|\overline{PQ}\times\overline{PR}|}{|\overline{PQ}||\overline{PR}|}=\dfrac{\sqrt{611}}{\sqrt{30}\sqrt{22}}\).

stem: If \(|\vec{a}|=5\), \(|\vec{b}|=13\) and \(|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|=25\), find \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}\).
solution: Given \(|\vec{a}\times\vec{b}|=25\). \(\therefore |\vec{a}|\cdot|\vec{b}|\sin\theta=25\) (\(\theta\) is the angle between \(\vec{a}\) and \(\vec{b}\)). \(5\times 13\sin\theta=25\) \(\therefore \sin\theta=\dfrac{25}{5\times13}=\dfrac{5}{13}\). \(\therefore \cos\theta=\sqrt{1-\sin^2\theta}=\sqrt{1-\dfrac{25}{169}}=\pm\dfrac{12}{13}\). \(\therefore \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=|\vec{a}|\cdot|\vec{b}|\cos\theta=5\times13\times\left(\pm\dfrac{12}{13}\right)=\pm 60\). Thus \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=60\) if \(0<\theta<\pi/2\) and \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=-60\) if \(\pi/2<\theta<\pi\).

stem: Direction ratios of two lines satisfy the relation \(2a-b+2c=0\) and \(ab+bc+ca=0\). Show that the lines are perpendicular.
solution: Given equations are \(2a-b+2c=0\) i.e. \(b=2a+2c\) ....(I) and \(ab+bc+ca=0\) ....(II). Put \(b=2a+2c\) in equation (II), we get \(a(2a+2c)+(2a+2c)c+ca=0\) i.e. \(2a^2+2ac+2ac+2c^2+ac=0\) i.e. \(2a^2+5ac+2c^2=0\) \(\therefore (2a+c)(a+2c)=0\). Case I: \(2a+c=0 \therefore 2a=-c\) ...(III). Using this, equation (I) becomes \(b=-c+2c=c\) i.e. \(b=c\) ...(IV). From (III) and (IV) we get \(\dfrac{a}{-1/2}=\dfrac{b}{1}=\dfrac{c}{1}\). Direction ratios of the 1st line are \(-\dfrac{1}{2},1,1\) i.e. \(-1,2,2=\vec{p}\) (say). Case II: \(a+2c=0 \therefore a=-2c\) ...(V). Using this, equation (I) becomes \(b=2(-2c)+2c=-2c\) i.e. \(b=-2c\) ...(VI). From (V) and (VI) we get \(\dfrac{a}{-2}=\dfrac{b}{-2}=\dfrac{c}{1}\). \(\therefore\) Direction ratios of the second line are \(-2,-2,1\) i.e. \(2,2,-1=\vec{q}\) (say). Now \(\vec{p}\cdot\vec{q}=(-1\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+2\hat{k})\cdot(2\hat{i}+2\hat{j}-\hat{k})=-2+4-2=0\). \(\therefore\) The lines are perpendicular.

stem: Find the direction cosines of the line which is perpendicular to the lines with direction ratios \(-1, 2, 2\) and \(0, 2, 1\).
solution: Given \(-1,2,2\) and \(0,2,1\) be direction ratios of lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\). Let \(l,m,n\) be direction cosines of line \(L\). As line \(L\) is perpendicular to lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\), then \(-l+2m+2n=0\) and \(2m+n=0\). From \(2m+n=0\), \(2m=-n\), \(\therefore \dfrac{m}{-1}=\dfrac{n}{2}\) ....(I). And \(-l+2m+2n=0\) becomes \(-l-n+2n=0\) i.e. \(-l+n=0\) i.e. \(l=n\), so \(\dfrac{l}{2}=\dfrac{n}{2}\) ....(II). From (I) and (II), \(\dfrac{l}{2}=\dfrac{m}{-1}=\dfrac{n}{2}\). The direction ratios of line L are \(2,-1,2\) and the direction cosines of line L are \(\dfrac{2}{3},\dfrac{-1}{3},\dfrac{2}{3}\).

stem: If M is the foot of the perpendicular drawn from A(4, 3, 2) on the line joining the points B(2, 4, 1) and C (4, 5, 3), find the coordinates of M.
solution: Let the point M divide BC internally in the ratio \(k:1\). \(\therefore M\equiv\left(\dfrac{4k+2}{k+1},\dfrac{5k+4}{k+1},\dfrac{3k+1}{k+1}\right)\) ....(I). \(\therefore\) Direction ratios of AM are \(\dfrac{4k+2}{k+1}-4,\dfrac{5k+4}{k+1}-3,\dfrac{3k+1}{k+1}-2=\vec{p}\) (say), i.e. \(\dfrac{-2}{k+1},\dfrac{2k+1}{k+1},\dfrac{k-1}{k+1}\), and direction ratios of BC are \(4-2,5-4,3-1\) i.e. \(2,1,2=\vec{q}\) (say). Since AM is perpendicular to BC, \(\vec{p}\cdot\vec{q}=0\) i.e. \(2\cdot\dfrac{(-2)}{k+1}+1\cdot\dfrac{(2k+1)}{k+1}+2\cdot\dfrac{(k-1)}{k+1}=0\) i.e. \(-4+2k+1+2k-2=0\) \(\therefore 4k-5=0\) \(\therefore k=\dfrac{5}{4}\). From (I), \(M\equiv\left(\dfrac{28}{9},\dfrac{41}{9},\dfrac{19}{9}\right)\).

solution:
The volume of the parallelepiped determined by \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}\) is the magnitude of their scalar triple product \(\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}\times\vec{c})\).

\(\vec{a}\cdot(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & 2 & 3 \\ -1 & 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = 1\begin{vmatrix}1&2\\1&4\end{vmatrix} - 2\begin{vmatrix}-1&2\\2&4\end{vmatrix} + 3\begin{vmatrix}-1&1\\2&1\end{vmatrix} = 1(4-2) - 2(-4-4) + 3(-1-2) = 9\)

Thus the volume of the parallelepiped is 9 cubic units.

So the volume of the parallelepiped is 1 cubic unit.

stem: Find the vector which is orthogonal to the vector \(3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\) and is coplanar with the vectors \(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
solution:
Let \(\vec{a}=3\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+6\hat{k}, \vec{b}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}, \vec{c}=\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).

Then by definition, a vector orthogonal to \(\vec{a}\) and coplanar to \(\vec{b}\) and \(\vec{c}\) is given by \(\vec{a}\times(\vec{b}\times\vec{c}) = (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c})\vec{b} - (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{c}\)

\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c} = 3(1)+2(-1)+6(1) = 7\), \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 3(2)+2(1)+6(1) = 14\)

\(= 7(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) - 14(\hat{i}-\hat{j}+\hat{k}) = 21\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}\)

stem: If \(\vec{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}, \vec{a}\cdot\vec{b}=1\) and \(\vec{a}\times\vec{b}=\hat{j}-\hat{k}\) then prove that \(\vec{b}=\hat{i}\).
solution:
\((\vec{a}\times\vec{b})\times\vec{a} = (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{a})\vec{b} - (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{a}\)

\(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{a} = |\vec{a}|^2 = 1+1+1 = 3\) and \(\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 1\)

\(\therefore (\hat{j}-\hat{k})\times(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) = 3(\vec{b}) - (\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})\)

\(i.e. \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = 3(\vec{b}) - (\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})\)

\((2\hat{i}-\hat{j}-\hat{k}) + (\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}) = 3\vec{b}\)

\(i.e.\ \hat{i} = \vec{b}\)

stem: Show that the points \(A(2,-1,0), B(-3,0,4), C(-1,-1,4)\) and \(D(0,-5,2)\) are non coplanar.
solution:
Let \(\vec{a}=2\hat{i}-\hat{j}, \vec{b}=-3\hat{i}+4\hat{k}, \vec{c}=-\hat{i}-\hat{j}+4\hat{k}, \vec{d}=-5\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\) be the position vectors of A, B, C, D respectively.

\(\overline{AB} = \vec{b}-\vec{a} = -5\hat{i}+\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\)

\(\overline{AC} = \vec{c}-\vec{a} = -3\hat{i}+4\hat{k}\)

\(\overline{AD} = \vec{d}-\vec{a} = -2\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\)

Consider: \(\overline{AB}\cdot(\overline{AC}\times\overline{AD}) = \begin{vmatrix} -5 & 1 & 4 \\ -3 & 0 & 4 \\ -2 & -4 & 2 \end{vmatrix}\)

\(= -5(0+16) - 1(-6+8) + 4(12)\)

\(= -80 - 2 + 48 = 34 \neq 0\)

Therefore, the points A, B, C, D are non-coplanar.

stem: If \(\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}\) are non coplanar vectors, then show that the four points \(2\vec{a}+\vec{b}, \vec{a}+2\vec{b}+\vec{c}, 4\vec{a}-2\vec{b}-\vec{c}\) and \(3\vec{a}+4\vec{b}-5\vec{c}\) are coplanar.
solution:
Let the 4 points be \(P(\vec{p}), Q(\vec{q}), R(\vec{r})\) and \(S(\vec{s})\) where

\(\vec{p} = 2\vec{a}+\vec{b}, \vec{q} = \vec{a}+2\vec{b}+\vec{c}, \vec{r} = 4\vec{a}-2\vec{b}-\vec{c}, \vec{s} = 3\vec{a}+4\vec{b}-5\vec{c}\)

Let us form 3 coinitial vectors:

\(\overline{PQ} = \vec{q}-\vec{p} = (\vec{a}+2\vec{b}+\vec{c}) - (2\vec{a}+\vec{b}) = -\vec{a}+\vec{b}+\vec{c}\)

\(\overline{PR} = \vec{r}-\vec{p} = (4\vec{a}-2\vec{b}-\vec{c}) - (2\vec{a}+\vec{b}) = 2\vec{a}-3\vec{b}-\vec{c}\)

\(\overline{PS} = \vec{s}-\vec{p} = (3\vec{a}+4\vec{b}-5\vec{c}) - (2\vec{a}+\vec{b}) = \vec{a}+3\vec{b}-5\vec{c}\)

P, Q, R, S are coplanar if and only if these three vectors \(\overline{PQ}, \overline{PR}\) and \(\overline{PS}\) are also coplanar; this is possible only if \(\overline{PQ}\cdot(\overline{PR}\times\overline{PS}) = 0\)

\(\overline{PQ}\cdot(\overline{PR}\times\overline{PS}) = \begin{vmatrix} -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & -1 \\ 1 & 3 & -5 \end{vmatrix} = -1(15+3) - 1(-10+1) + 1(6+3) = -18+9+9 = 0\)
